The problem

Good care gets lost in bad paperwork.

Behavioral health runs on documentation no one has time for. Clinicians write after hours. Denials arrive months later, over a line nobody wrote. Auditors ask for a rule you didn't know applied to your state. The work was done — the record just couldn't prove it.

◷

The after-hours tax

Notes written at 9pm from memory are thinner, later, and harder to defend — and they are the reason good clinicians burn out and leave.

⊘

Denials for missing words

Care that clearly happened gets refused because the record didn't say the specific thing a payer needed to see, in the way they needed to see it.

§

Rules that move

What's required depends on your state, your license, and your level of care — and it changes. Most systems leave that entirely to you to remember.

What Kura does

The record keeps up with the care.

Not a filing cabinet with a login. Kura understands what your programs are required to document, watches the chart as care happens, and tells you what's missing while it can still be fixed.

Documentation that starts itself

With consent, a session becomes a structured draft in your own clinical voice — so you start from a working note, not a blank page. You review, correct, and sign. The signature is always yours.

  • ✓ Every AI output is a draft that requires a clinician's signature
  • ✓ Nothing is asserted that the record doesn't support
  • ✓ Typing it yourself is always a first-class path

Compliance you can see, before the auditor does

Kura tracks each chart against what actually applies to it — your state, your program, that patient's level of care — and shows the gaps in plain language while the episode is still open.

  • ✓ Requirements shown with the rule behind them, not folklore
  • ✓ Gaps surface early, when they're still fixable
  • ✓ Readiness is a live number, not a fire drill

Built to defend the claim

When a payer asks why care was necessary, the answer should already exist. Kura assembles the clinical story from the record itself — the thread from assessment to plan to progress — and a clinician signs what goes out.

  • ✓ Evidence drawn from the chart, never invented
  • ✓ Authorizations and deadlines tracked, not remembered
  • ✓ Kura never submits on your behalf — a human always signs
Designed per role

Everyone opens Kura to their own job.

A front-desk day and a clinical day have nothing in common, so they shouldn't share a screen. Each role gets a workspace built around its actual work — and sees only what that work requires.

Clinicians & nurses

The day's care, the charts that need you, and documentation that starts itself.

Front desk

The schedule, registration, and the details that are theirs to own — without clinical content.

Intake & admissions

Every inquiry from first call to admitted, with priority handled the way the funding requires.

Case management

Referrals, coordination, and the follow-through that decides whether care actually continues.

Billing & utilization

Coverage, authorizations, and payer work — with the clinical evidence a review actually needs.

Directors & QA

Oversight, outcomes, supervision queues, and audit readiness as a standing number.

Trust

Behavioral health has stricter rules. We built for them first.

Substance-use records carry federal protections beyond ordinary health privacy, and a system that treats them like any other note puts the clinic at risk. Kura was designed around those obligations rather than retrofitted to them.

42 CFRPart 2 protections modeled as architecture, not a checkbox
SignedEvery clinical artifact carries a human signature and a full history
RecordedEvery view, edit, and disclosure is logged and answerable
Least accessRole-scoped by design — including for us as your vendor

The clinician stays the author

AI drafts, ranks, and explains. It never signs, never decides care, and never asserts what the record can't support. The clinical judgment — and the accountability — remain human, always.

Sensitive charts stay sensitive

Employee and VIP charts can be sealed from ordinary view, with a documented, time-limited path for anyone who genuinely needs access. Privacy that survives contact with a real clinic.
